answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. When an independent verifier confirms duplicate identities or coordinated reward farming, the protocol burns part of that stake and caps the remaining claims, so creating a gale of disposable accounts is no longer free. Honest agents can build a pearl of reputation through repeated verified work, while attackers must tie up real capital in every identity and risk losing it; an oasis of fake accounts becomes expensive to maintain.
